name: Fujifilm Neopan 400 Presto
notes: Japanese Product Information Bulletin 'ネオパン 400 PRESTO (135)', 4 pages, vector drawings. Document 163AR0120A; the date is read from the print code 神Q-07-7-FP next to the reference number on page 4 (2007, July) and is not stated otherwise. Speed ISO 400/27 deg, orthopanchromatic.

curves: page 4, section 10 (特性曲線), three plots, all 20 C small round tank. x axis is log H in lux-seconds as printed; the frames run from -3.5 to 1.5 although the labels stop at 1.0 (grid lines every 0.5; calibrated on them), y is density 0 to 3.0. Exposure light and densitometry are not stated. Printed average gradients (G-bar): SPD 9 min 0.83, 5 min 45 s 0.65, 4 min 15 s 0.53; Microfine 11 min 0.64, 8 min 30 s 0.53, 7 min 0.41; D-76 12 min 0.83, 8 min 45 s 0.65, 7 min 30 s 0.54.

v is SPD 4 min 15 s (stored as 4.25): page 2 lists スーパープロドール (SPD) first and gives EI 400 at 20 C as 4 1/4 min; the other SPD times are v-spd-9 and v-spd-5.75 (plot 'curves'). A plot name can be used once per sheet, so Microfine is the extra plot 'curves-microfine' (v-microfine-11, -8.5, -7) and D-76 is 'curves-d76' (v-d76-12, -8.75, -7.5); build.py reads only 'curves'. By the page 2 table the EI 400 times at 20 C are SPD 4 1/4, Microfine 7 and D-76 7 1/2 min, i.e. the lowest curve of each plot; the other curves of each plot are the longer (push-processed) developments.

Curves are the vector paths themselves (one path per curve, 25 points), so the traces follow them exactly; they start at the left frame (log H -3.5, base plus fog plateau about 0.2) and end at log H about 0.7, inside the G-bar labels (labels are drawn beside the curves and did not disturb the trace). The three curves of a plot coincide below log H about -2.8.

sensitivity: page 4, section 11 (分光感度曲線), daylight 5400 K, a plotted curve (single path). The axis 比感度(対数) (relative sensitivity, log) has no numbers, only an arrow marking 1.0 log unit between two grid lines; y here is relative, with the lower grid line taken as 0.0 and the upper as 1.0 (zero point arbitrary). The curve runs from about 391 nm to about 650 nm and ends in a near-vertical drop at about 645 nm, so the last 5 nm samples are approximate.
Grain: no granularity (RMS) value or resolving power is printed in this sheet. Page 4 section 12 has development time vs G-bar curves (not traced); page 3 has automatic processor conditions.
